questions.stem: Why does the woman wish to study architecture?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士为什么希望学习建筑学?
questions.answerText: She is drawn to its integration of design and engineering.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: In particular, I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering. 尤其是，我被设计与工程的结合所吸引。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者直接应答动机。教授先问 Why did you choose it?，她的回答里用 I'm attracted to 直接给出动机，且以 In particular 加重强调——"问因 + 被问者亲口应答 + 加重语气"三重 信号锁定此句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: the marriage of design and engineering ↔its integration of design and engineering marriage=integration同义改写

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 录音确有 I'm attracted to，A 项 She is attracted to the beauty of modern buildings. 借用了 attracted 这个原词，但她被吸引的是"设计与工程的结合"，不是"现代建筑的 美"——美这一点录音从未说，属听到 attracted 就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering B) 原词陷阱 preoccupied 一词录音里出现在教授口中 you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics，指她曾为数学发愁，根本不是"痴迷当建筑师的梦想"。B 项 She is preoccupied with her dream to be an architect. 盗了 preoccupied 又改了对象，与 问"动机"无关。 借用原文：you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics C) 未提及 C 项 She is influenced by her father who teaches architecture. 牵出一个"教建筑的父 亲"，但整段录音从未提到她父亲，更没说受其影响——是预读时就警惕的"凭空多出一个人 物"的诱选。

options.label: A
options.text: She is attracted to the beauty of modern buildings.
options.textZh: 她被现代建筑的美感所吸引。

options.label: B
options.text: She is preoccupied with her dream to be an architect.
options.textZh: 她一心想着成为建筑师的梦想。

options.label: C
options.text: She is influenced by her father who teaches architecture.
options.textZh: 她受到教授建筑学的父亲的影响。

options.label: D
options.text: She is drawn to its integration of design and engineering.
options.textZh: 她被建筑学中设计与工程的结合所吸引。

questions.stem: How does the woman say she will overcome the difficulty in learning mathematics?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士说她将如何克服学习数学的困难?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Math might be the toughest subject I encounter in the curriculum, but I'll simply put in the work required. 数学可能是我在课程里遇到的最难的科目，但我会直接付出所需的努力。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 转折 but 后才是真应对。她先承认 Math might be the toughest subject，紧接 but I'll simply put in the work required——转折词 but 之后才是她真正给出的克服办法，前半 只是铺垫难处。"but 后是落点"是听力定位的硬信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: put in the work required ↔Through hard work put in work=hard work同义概括

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 未提及 对话里确有 professor 这个人，B 项 With the professor's help. 借"现场有教授"诱你选， 但她讲克服数学的办法时只字未提靠教授，靠的是自己出力——属"同场有这人就误以为靠 他"的陷阱。 C) 原词陷阱 录音里 I was doing some online research 确实出现 online，C 项 By studying the subject online. 盗了 online。但她上网只是"做了点调研"判断自己应付得来，并非"靠网上 学数学"来克服难点——原词在、用途被偷换。 借用原文：I was doing some online research D) 未提及 D 项 By taking prerequisite courses. 说靠"修先修课"克服，但录音从未提到 prerequisite 或先修课程这回事——是凭空安上的办法。

options.label: A
options.textZh: 通过刻苦学习。

options.label: B
options.textZh: 在教授的帮助下。

options.label: C
options.textZh: 通过在线学习该科目。

options.label: D
options.textZh: 通过修读先修课程。

questions.stem: What does the man say about architects' contribution to a city?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士对建筑师对城市的贡献有何看法?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: And the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals. 而且你所建造的那些遗产，会比我们这些凡人存续得久得多。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 男士对城市贡献的直接断言。男士谈到 the contribution you make to a city 后，紧接断 言 the legacies you build will last much longer——这句直接定性"建筑师留下的东西能 存续很久"，是他对该话题的正面陈述句，定位于此。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: will last much longer than any of us mortals ↔It is long-lasting last much longer=long-lasting同义

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 A 项 It is groundbreaking."具开创性"在录音里毫无对应——男士谈的是贡献能"长久存 续"，不是"开天辟地"，属凭空贴标签。 C) 与原文相反 录音里 Due to its material nature 出现 material（实体的），C 项 It is immaterial. 恰好 取了它的反义 immaterial（非物质/无关紧要）。建筑明明是"实体"，选项却说"无形"， 是"盗原词又反极性"的诱选。 借用原文：Due to its material nature D) 原词陷阱 录音 longer than any of us mortals 用 mortals（凡人）作对比，D 项 It is immortal. 盗 这个词根改成 immortal（不朽）。原文只说贡献"比凡人活得久"，是相对的"更久"，并 非"永不灭"——把相对的久夸成绝对不朽，程度过头。 借用原文：will last much longer than any of us mortals

options.label: A
options.textZh: 它是开创性的。

options.label: B
options.textZh: 它是持久的。

options.label: C
options.textZh: 它是无关紧要的。

options.label: D
options.textZh: 它是不朽的。

questions.stem: What subject does the man suggest the woman start with?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士建议这位女士从什么科目开始学习?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Nevertheless, I would suggest you start with computer science because there will be many intricate visuals you will have to produce as part of your projects. 不过，我建议你从计算机科学开始，因为你的项目里会有很多复杂的图像需要你来制作。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: Nevertheless 转折 + suggest start with。前句先泛举 philosophy and economics 等 领域，再用 Nevertheless 一转，紧跟 I would suggest you start with computer science ——转折后的"建议 + start with"双信号，直指真正要先学的那门。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I would suggest you start with computer science ↔Computer science 原句点名即选项学科

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 philosophy and economics 里 economics 被念到，但那是男士泛举"大学会鼓励你学的各 类领域"，A 项 Economics. 盗这个原词冒充答案；题问的是 start with（先学），经济学并 非他建议起步的那门。 借用原文：fields as wide-ranging as philosophy and economics B) 原词陷阱 B 项 Philosophy. 同样来自 philosophy and economics 的泛举，philosophy 被念到却不 是"建议先学"的那门——与 A 一样是"听到学科名就想划"的原词诱选。 借用原文：fields as wide-ranging as philosophy and economics D) 答非所问 录音末尾 the history of Western art 确出现"西方艺术"，D 项 Western art. 盗了它。但那 是男士另起一句"还建议你尽量多学美术"，与本题问的 start with（最先入手）不是同一件 事——位置和性质都对不上。 借用原文：another thing that I would recommend you learn as much as you can is fine arts, in particular, the history of Western art 1 W: So as I mentioned over the phone, we are looking for someone who is very discreet, I can't stress this enough. W: 就像我在电话里提到的，我们在找一个非常谨慎的人，这点我怎么强调都不为过。 2 M: I fully understand. M: 我完全理解。 3 W: As we all know, being such a famous football player at Real Madrid, Mr. Sanchez has a very high public profile. This means he cannot leave the house without being recognized and harassed. W: 众所周知，作为Real Madrid这么有名的足球运动员，Sanchez先生的公众知名度非常高。这意味着他 一出门就会被认出来，被骚扰。 4 M: Yes, I completely understand how imperative it would be to respect Mr. Sanchez's private life. M: 是的，我完全明白尊重Sanchez先生的私人生活有多重要。 5 W: Good. As his personal assistant, you would be required to run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez, things he cannot do himself due to his fame, like going to the supermarket or post office. So, well, at first sight it may appear that working for a celebrity is very glamorous. Nothing could be further from the truth. I'm telling you this so that you don't get any false expectations of what the job has to offer you. W: 很好。作为他的私人助理，你需要为Sanchez先生处理一些日常琐事，那些他因为名气而没法亲自做 的事，比如去超市或邮局。所以，嗯，乍一看为名人工作可能显得很光鲜亮丽。但事实恰恰相反。我告诉 你这些是为了让你对这份工作能给你带来什么不要有错误的期待。 6 M: Thanks. I understand this too. This is my first job after graduating from university. So frankly, I don't have much prior working experience. I am, however, very excited about the prospect of joining this Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. company and very keen to start from the bottom in whatever capacity I may be of use. M: 谢谢。我也明白这点。这是我大学毕业后的第一份工作。所以坦白说，我之前没什么工作经验。不 过，我对加入这家公司的前景非常兴奋，也非常渴望从基层做起，无论我能在什么岗位上发挥作用。 7 W: That's good to hear. You sound very energetic. Tell me why you think you are well suited for this job? W: 很高兴听到这个。你听起来很有活力。跟我说说你为什么觉得自己很适合这份工作? 8 M: Well, firstly, I love football. I'm a lifelong Real Madrid supporter and go to their games every weekend I can. I would simply love to have a job where I'm involved in some capacity with Real Madrid, regardless of the position and salary. And secondly, I think what this company does in sports consultancy is very cool. And I think my language skills could prove very useful down the road. M: 嗯，首先，我热爱足球。我是Real Madrid的终身球迷，每个周末只要有空就去看他们的比赛。我真的 很想有一份工作能让我以某种方式参与到Real Madrid中，不管是什么职位和薪水。其次，我觉得贵公司 在体育咨询方面做的事情非常酷。而且我觉得我的语言技能将来可能会很有用。 9 W: Please tell me more about your language skills. W: 请多说说你的语言技能。 10 M: I am fully fluent in English and Spanish and have a working proficiency in French. M: 我的英语和西班牙语都很流利，法语也有工作水平。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the conversation about Mr. Sanchez?
questions.stemZh: 从对话中我们了解到关于桑切斯先生的什么信息?
questions.answerText: He is well known to the public.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: As we all know, being such a famous football player at Real Madrid, Mr. Sanchez has a very high public profile. This means he cannot leave the house without being recognized and harassed. 众所周知，作为皇马一名如此有名的足球运动员，桑切斯先生有着很高的公众知名度。这意 味着他一出门就会被认出、被骚扰。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 直接的身份介绍句。女士用 being such a famous football player at Real Madrid 一句话 给桑切斯定了身份，再用 has a very high public profile 说明其名气之大——这种"客观介 绍人物"的陈述句就是身份细节题的答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: has a very high public profile ↔well known to the public 「高公众知名度」=「被公众熟知」

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 He has occasionally been harassed by his fans. 借了录音 recognized and harassed 里 的 harassed 一词，但录音说的是"一出门就"被骚扰、且并未限定"被粉丝"，更没说"偶 尔"。题问的是"我们了解到什么"，最核心是他名气大，A把附带后果当主答案、还加了 occasionally,fans 这些原文没有的限定。 借用原文：recognized and harassed B) 张冠李戴 He has been guarded by a discreet assistant. 把开头 we are looking for someone who is very discreet 里的 discreet 拿来，安成"他被一位谨慎的助理护卫"。但 discreet 是 对应聘者（男方）的要求，不是说桑切斯有这样一个助理——人物对应被搬错，且题问的是 桑切斯本人，不是他的助理。 借用原文：someone who is very discreet D) 偷换概念 He is a famous football coach. 借用了录音 famous football player 里的 famous football，却把 player（球员）偷换成 coach（教练）。一字之差、身份全错，这正是预读 时圈出"coach 是差异点"要防的偷换。 借用原文：famous football player

options.label: A
options.text: He has occasionally been harassed by his fans.
options.textZh: 他偶尔会被粉丝骚扰。

options.label: B
options.text: He has been guarded by a discreet assistant.
options.textZh: 他一直由一位谨慎的助理保护着。

options.label: C
options.text: He is well known to the public.
options.textZh: 他为公众所熟知。

options.label: D
options.text: He is a famous football coach.
options.textZh: 他是一位著名的足球教练。

questions.stem: What will the man do if he gets the job?
questions.stemZh: 如果男士得到这份工作,他会做什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: As his personal assistant, you would be required to run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez, things he cannot do himself due to his fame, like going to the supermarket or post office. 作为他的私人助理，你将被要求为桑切斯先生跑日常琐事，那些他因名气太大而无法自己做 的事，比如去超市或邮局。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 招聘者直接交代岗位。女方用 As his personal assistant 一句明确点出岗位名，这种由招聘 方直接交代"你将担任什么"的句子，就是"他将做什么"的答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: As his personal assistant ↔Serve as a personal assistant. 「作为私人助理」=「担任私人助理」

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 过度推断 Play a key role in Real Madrid. 借了第7、8段反复出现的 Real Madrid，把"跑腿助理"夸 成"在皇马担任关键角色"。录音清楚说他要做的是 run common everyday chores（跑日 常琐事），与"key role"完全相反，是过度拔高。 借用原文：run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez C) 张冠李戴 Run common daily chores for the woman. 几乎照搬录音 run common everyday chores，只把"for Mr. Sanchez"换成"for the woman"。跑腿是为桑切斯、不是为这位招聘 的女士，服务对象被掉包——正是预读时圈 for the woman 要防的张冠李戴。 借用原文：run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez D) 与原文相反 Help promote Mr. Sanchez's public profile. 拿了 high public profile 里的 public profile，编成"帮桑切斯提升公众形象"。但录音说的是因他名气太大、助理替他做他没法做 的事（things he cannot do himself due to his fame），是"避开曝光"，绝非"提升曝 光"，方向相反。 借用原文：has a very high public profile

options.textZh: 担任私人助理。

options.label: B
options.text: Play a key role in Real Madrid.
options.textZh: 在皇家马德里扮演关键角色。

options.label: C
options.text: Run common daily chores for the woman.
options.textZh: 为女士处理日常琐事。

questions.stem: What does the man say about himself?
questions.stemZh: 男士如何评价自己?
questions.answerText: He has little previous work experience.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: This is my first job after graduating from university. So frankly, I don't have much prior working experience. 这是我大学毕业后的第一份工作。所以坦白说，我没有多少之前的工作经验。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 第一人称的自我坦白。男方用 This is my first job after graduating from university 加 I don't have much prior working experience 直陈自身处境，这种"I/my"领起的自述句即 本题答案落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I don't have much prior working experience ↔He has little previous work experience. 「没多少经验」=「几乎没经验」

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 过度推断 He is honest and always tells the truth. 大概由录音里 frankly（坦白说）联想而来，但 frankly 只是说话的语气词，男方并未谈自己"诚实、总说真话"。把一个口头副词夸成性格 优点，属无中生有的推断。 借用原文：So frankly, I don't have much prior working experience B) 未提及 He once worked part-time in university. 用了 university 这个录音确实出现的词（after graduating from university），但男方只说"大学毕业"，从未提"在校期间打过工"。借眼 熟的 university 编出一段没说过的经历，属未提及。 借用原文：after graduating from university C) 未提及 He cares little about his working hours. 听起来像呼应他"愿从底层做起"（keen to start from the bottom）的谦逊，但他谈的是不计职位与薪水，从没说"不在乎工作时长 （working hours）"。working hours 是录音里完全没出现的话题。

options.label: A
options.text: He is honest and always tells the truth.
options.textZh: 他诚实且总是说真话。

options.label: B
options.text: He once worked part-time in university.
options.textZh: 他曾在大学期间做过兼职工作。

options.label: C
options.text: He cares little about his working hours.
options.textZh: 他不太在意自己的工作时间。

options.label: D
options.text: He has little previous work experience.
options.textZh: 他几乎没有以前的工作经验。

questions.stem: Why does the man think he is a very competitive candidate?
questions.stemZh: 男士为什么认为自己是一位非常有竞争力的候选人?
questions.answerText: He has a high proficiency in several languages.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: And I think my language skills could prove very useful down the road. 而且我觉得我的语言能力日后会很有用。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 他自陈的优势落点。在列举理由的段落里，男方以 I think my language skills could prove very useful 把"语言能力"点为自己的可用之长——这种"I think my … useful"的自夸句 就是优势题的答案句。第10段又用 fully fluent in English and Spanish 坐实他确有多语 能力。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: my language skills could prove very useful ↔He has a high proficiency in several languages. 「语言能力有用」=「精通几门语言」

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 He has a strong ability to connect with people. 描述的人际沟通能力，录音通篇没有提 及。他列的是爱足球、觉得公司酷、语言能力，没有任何一句谈"与人连接"，属凭"助理该会 沟通"的常识脑补。 C) 张冠李戴 He has a sound knowledge of sports consultancy. 盗用了录音 what this company does in sports consultancy 里的 sports consultancy。但这是他在夸"公司做的体育咨询 很酷"，说的是公司的业务，不是他本人懂体育咨询——把公司的事安成了他的能力。 借用原文：what this company does in sports consultancy is very cool D) 未提及 He has a natural capacity to cooperate with others. 和A一样属人际类能力，与他亲口列 的"语言能力"无关，录音没说他"善于与人协作"。它和A刻意做得相像（connect with people/cooperate with others），用来分散对正确项B的注意。 Section B 1 Adventure sports are undeniably attractive to many energetic and thrill-seeking kids. Sports like rock climbing, surfing, skiing, and mountain biking, thus have lots of appeal. They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity. 冒险运动对许多精力充沛、寻求刺激的孩子来说无疑具有吸引力。因此，攀岩、冲浪、滑雪和山地自行车 等运动颇具魅力。它们没有传统团队运动的诸多规则和压力，但仍然具备户外体育活动的所有益处。 2 When properly supervised, extreme sports can be a part of a healthy, balanced life. Some adventure sports may be associated with high risks of injury, so it's important for kids to figure out when to take risks, and when not to. Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears. But to some, these very risks are what makes these sports a bad choice. New research suggests cyberloafing can help workers cope with an exceptionally stressful work environment. 大多数关于网络闲逛的研究都侧重于通过网络监控和计算机使用政策等干预措施来防止员工从事这种行 为。但事实证明,这类行为可能并不意味着员工懒惰或只是在浪费时间。工作中使用社交媒体与员工敬业度 和工作满意度的提高有关。新研究表明,网络闲逛可以帮助员工应对压力极大的工作环境。 3 But is cyberloafing actually effective at reducing employee stress levels? Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini-break, giving employees an opportunity to recover from stressful work situations. To test this, we asked workers to complete an online survey and rank how much time they spent cyberloafing, checking Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. non-work emails and shopping. We also asked them to rank job satisfaction, their desire to quit, and how often they've experienced mistreatment at work, such as being bullied, threatened or yelled at. A) When psychologist Jessica Pryor lived near an internationally renowned university, she once saw a student walking into a library holding a sleeping bag and a coffee maker. She has heard of graduate students spending 12 to 18 hours at a time in the lab. B) Along with other therapists, Pryor, who is now with the Family Institute at Northwestern University, is trying to sound the alarm about a tendency among young adults and college students to strive for perfection in their work—sometimes at any cost. Though it is often portrayed as a positive trait, Pryor and others say extreme perfectionism can lead to depression, anxiety, and even suicide.
C) What's more, perfectionism seems to be on the rise. In a study of thousands of American, Canadian, and British college students published earlier this year, Thomas Curran of the University of Bath and Andrew Hill of York St. John University found that today's college students report higher levels of perfectionism than college students did during the 1990s or early 2000s. They measured three types of perfectionism: self-oriented, or a desire to be perfect; socially prescribed, or a desire to live up to others' expectations; and other-oriented, or holding others to unrealistic standards. "One of the most common things couples argue about is the proper way of loading the dishwasher," says Amy Bach, a psychologist in Providence, Rhode Island.
E) Curran describes socially prescribed perfectionism as "My self-esteem is contingent on what other people think." His study didn't examine the causal reasons for its rise, but he assumes that the rise of both standardized testing and social media might play a role. These days, LinkedIn alerts us when our rival gets a new job, and Instagram can let us know how well "liked" our lives are compared with a friend's. In an opinion piece earlier this year, Curran and Hill argue that society has also become more dog-eat-dog. P1 How on earth did we come to this? We protect our children obsessively from every harm; we scrutinize every carer, teacher or doctor with whom they come into contact. Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access.

P2 We seem to take it for granted that advertisers and marketers are allowed to condition even the youngest children. Before children have even developed a proper sense of their own identity, or learned to handle money, they're encouraged to associate status and self-worth with stuff, and to look to external things such as fame and wealth for validation. We're turning out little consumers rather than young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live.

P3 We've reached this point so gradually that many of us have never questioned it. It's crept up on us in the 60 years since advertisers started to target the young and found that they could recruit them to a commercial assault on their parents. We've come to know it as "pester power" or the ability of children to pressure parents to make certain purchases.

P4 Many psychologists, child development experts and educators point to research suggesting that this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism is contributing to growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness.

P5 Not all psychologists agree. There're plenty working hand in glove with a ￡12bn-a-year industry that has turned the manipulation of adult emotions and desires into an art form—often literally. It's also one that's forever developing new ways to persuade our children to desire material possessions, and because of advertisements' viral effect they only need to infect a few to reach the many. Advertising and marketing can serve a useful purpose for children. Marketing may help socialize children as consumers, inform them about products, and help them carve out unique identities as they reach adulthood.

P6 Then, should we ban all advertising aimed at young children? I say yes.

P7 Of course there'll be plenty of objections to an outright ban on advertising to the under-11s. There'll be those who argue that would be a breach of freedom of speech and infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products.

P8 Most parents hate what advertising does to their children, but we do have the power to end it and let our children grow up free from many of the pressures of consumerism until they're old enough to make their own decisions. And though advertising is only part of an all-pervasive( 无处不在的) marketing culture we need to make a start somewhere. Let's ban all advertising targeting children of primary school age and younger now.

reading-2.raw:
P1 Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent dehumanizing effect it has and the relentless pressure it brings. But it's on the rise around the world as firms look to become more efficient by squeezing more productivity from their workers. More than half of companies with over $750m in annual revenue used "non-traditional" monitoring techniques on staff last year.

P2 Monitoring employee performance gives firms the ability to assess how their staff are performing and interacting, which can be good for both the firm and employees themselves. A growing number of analytics companies offer this service. They gather "data exhaust" left by employees' email and instant messaging apps, and use name badges equipped with radio-frequency identification devices and microphones. These can check how much time you spend talking, your volume and tone of voice, even if you do not dominate conversations. While this may sound intrusive, exponents argue that it can also protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment. 

P3 Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis.

P4 Over the last few years a Stockholm co-working space called Epicenter has gone much further and holds popular "chipping parties", where people can have microchips implanted in their hands. They can use the implants to access electronically-controlled doors, or monitor how typing speed correlates with heart rate. Implanted chips may seem extreme, but it is a relatively small step from ID cards and biometrics to such devices.

P5 As long as such schemes are voluntary, there will probably be a growing number of convenience-oriented uses so that a substantial number of workers would opt to have a chip inserted. But if implanted chips are used to reduce slack time or rest breaks, that could prove to be detrimental. And if surveillance tools take away autonomy, that's when they prove most unpopular. A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged.

P6 If bosses don't communicate effectively, employees assume the worst. But if they're open about the information they're collecting and what they're doing with it, research suggests 46% of employees are generally okay with it. Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staffers remain sceptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.

P7 So workplace surveillance could be empowering for staff and useful for companies looking to become more efficient and profitable. But implemented in the wrong way, it could also become an unpopular tool of oppression that proves counterproductive.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “When faced with differing opinions, we should try to reach agreement through friendly discussion and reasonable argument.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words(not including the sentence given).
writing.model: When faced with differing opinions, we should try to reach agreement through friendly discussion and reasonable argument. In a world where people come from diverse backgrounds, disagreements are inevitable; yet how we handle them reveals our maturity. Rather than shouting others down or stubbornly clinging to our own views, seeking common ground through calm reasoning is always the wiser choice. The reason is simple: friendly discussion invites cooperation, while quarrels only deepen the divide. Take the famous debates in scientific communities. When Darwin proposed his theory of evolution, opponents raised sharp objections, but progress was made not by insults but by patient argument and shared evidence. Similarly, in my own study group, a heated dispute over a project was resolved only after we sat down, listened to one another, and combined our ideas. Mutual respect turned rivals into partners. In conclusion, differing opinions need not lead to conflict. If we approach them with an open mind, sound logic, and genuine respect, we can transform disagreement into understanding and reach a consensus that benefits everyone. This is not only a skill but a mark of a civilized society.
writing.modelZh: 【参考译文】面对不同的意见时，我们应当努力通过友好的讨论和合理的论证来达成一致。在一个人们来自不同背景的世界里，分歧不可避免；然而我们如何处理分歧，恰恰显露出我们的成熟。与其压制他人或固执己见，不如通过冷静的说理去寻求共识，这永远是更明智的选择。道理很简单：友好的讨论邀来合作，而争吵只会加深隔阂。以科学界那些著名的争论为例。当达尔文提出进化论时，反对者提出了尖锐的质疑，但真正推动进步的不是谩骂，而是耐心的论证与共享的证据。同样，在我自己的学习小组里，一场因项目而起的激烈争执，只有在我们坐下来、互相倾听、把彼此的想法结合起来之后才得以化解。相互尊重把对手变成了伙伴。总而言之，不同的意见不必导致冲突。如果我们以开放的心态、严谨的逻辑和真诚的尊重去面对它们，就能把分歧转化为理解，达成惠及每个人的共识。这不仅是一种能力，更是一个文明社会的标志。【第 1 段】照抄首句加背景态度双句。开头逐字照抄给定首句 When faced with differing opinions...

outline.text: 照抄首句加背景态度双句。开头逐字照抄给定首句 When faced with differing opinions... reasonable argument.，随即用 In a world where people come from diverse backgrounds, disagreements are inevitable 补背景、用 Rather than shouting others down... is always the wiser choice 亮态度，落实第一段‘照抄首句并亮明立场’的功能。

理由加达尔文例加小组亲历。先用 The reason is simple: friendly discussion invites cooperation, while quarrels only deepen the divide 给理由，再以 When Darwin proposed his theory of evolution... 上名人例，用 Similarly, in my own study group 接亲身经历，末句 Mutual respect turned rivals into partners 小结回扣中心，兑现‘论证＋举例’的主体段功能。

重申加条件句加点睛升华。以 In conclusion, differing opinions need not lead to conflict 重申，用 If we approach them with an open mind, sound logic, and genuine respect, we can transform disagreement into understanding 条件句复用首句关键词回扣，末句升华到 a mark of a civilized society，形成首尾闭环。

translation.reference: With the rapid development of China's economy and the steady improvement of people's living standards, urban residents are placing increasingly high demands on the environment and the quality of life. To meet these rising demands, Chinese local governments are attaching greater importance to the construction and improvement of public facilities. By building new squares, parks and public green spaces, or redesigning and renovating existing public areas, many cities have provided their citizens with more places for leisure and social activities. Today, government-funded fitness equipment and newly paved fitness trails can be seen everywhere in many cities, which has not only markedly improved the conditions for residents' outdoor activities but also made the cities more beautiful.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主语=城市居民,谓语=要求越来越高（主语策略：原句主语） 中文已给出明确主语 城市居民对环境和生活品质的要求越来越高,直接用它作英文主语:urban residents。主干立为 urban residents have increasingly high expectations / demand more and more,宾语是 for the environment and quality of life。句首 随着中国经济的快速发展和人 们生活水平的稳步提高 是背景,不进主干。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 随着…→With 引导的伴随状语 随着中国经济的快速发展和人们生活水平的稳步提高 不是主干,降级成 With 引导的介词短语作状 语:With the rapid development of China's economy and the steady improvement of people's living standards,置于句首,后接主句。两个并列的'发展/提高'用 and 连接两个名词短语, 而非各起一个分句,避免拖成流水句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时:demand / have expectations,陈述当下普遍现状。 单复数 城市居民不止一人→urban residents 用复数;相应谓语用复数 have / demand。 程度词 '越来越高'是递增,用 increasingly high 或 more and more,别只译成 high 丢掉'越来越'的递增 义。 搭配 '对…的要求'用 demand for sth 或 expectations for / of sth,介词搭配固定,别用 require to。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: With the rapid development of China's economy and the steady improvement of people's living standards, urban residents are placing increasingly high demands on the environment and the quality of life. 2. 中国地方政府更加注重公共设施的建设和改进,以更好地满足人们的需求。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主语=地方政府,谓语=注重建设和改进（主语策略：原句主语） 中国地方政府更加注重公共设施的建设和改进 主语明确是'地方政府',直接作英文主语 local governments;谓语 pay more attention to / attach greater importance to;宾语是'公共设施的 建设和改进'。句末 以更好地满足人们的需求 是目的,不进主干。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 以…→to do 目的状语 以更好地满足人们的需求 表目的,降级成不定式 to better meet people's needs 作目的状语,接在 主句后。'建设和改进'两个并列名词作 to 的宾语:the construction and improvement of public facilities,不必拆成两个分句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指基调用一般现在时:local governments pay / attach,陈述当前做法。 单复数 '地方政府'指各地多个政府→local governments 用复数,谓语随之用复数 pay / attach。 搭配 '注重'用 attach (greater) importance to / pay more attention to,后接名词;'满足需求'用 meet/satisfy one's needs,needs 用复数。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Chinese local governments are attaching greater importance to the construction and improvement of public facilities in order to better meet people's needs. 3. 通过兴建新的广场、公园和公共绿地或对原有公共场地重新加以规划改造,许多城市为市民提 供了更多休闲和社交的场所。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主语=许多城市,谓语=提供了场所（主语策略：原句主语） 许多城市为市民提供了更多休闲和社交的场所 主语是'许多城市'→many cities,谓语 provide / offer,宾语 more places for leisure and social activities。句首一大串 通过兴建新的广场、公园和 公共绿地或对原有公共场地重新加以规划改造 是方式,不进主干。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 通过…→By doing 方式状语 通过兴建新的广场、公园和公共绿地或对原有公共场地重新加以规划改造 译成 By 引导的动名词方 式状语:By building new squares, parks and public green spaces, or redesigning and renovating existing public areas。其中'兴建……'与'重新规划改造……'是两种并列方式,用 or 连接 两个 doing 结构;'广场、公园和公共绿地'是三个并列宾语,A, B and C 列举。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 '提供了'带完成义,可用现在完成时 have provided 强调已带来的结果;若与全篇统一也可用一般现在 时 provide。本句宜用 have provided,既不悖基调又点出'已经提供'的完成感。 单复数 广场/公园/绿地都不止一处→squares, parks, public green spaces 全用复数;'许多城市'→many cities;'场所'→places 复数。 结构平行 or 连接的两个方式须同形:building… 对 redesigning and renovating…,都用 -ing 动名词,别一个 -ing 一个 to do。 搭配 '为…提供…'用 provide sb with sth 或 provide sth for sb;'休闲和社交的场所'→places for leisure and social activities。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: By building new squares, parks and public green spaces, or redesigning and renovating existing public areas, many cities have provided their citizens with more places for leisure and social activities. 4. 如今,政府出资购置的健身器械和铺设的健身步道在不少城市随处可见,既明显改善了市民户外 活动的条件,又使城市更加美丽。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主语=健身器械和健身步道,谓语=随处可见（主语策略：原句主语） 政府出资购置的健身器械和铺设的健身步道在不少城市随处可见 的主语是'健身器械和健身步 道'→fitness equipment and fitness trails,谓语'随处可见'→can be seen everywhere / are commonly seen。'政府出资购置的''铺设的'是修饰主语的定语,不进主干;句末 既明显改善了市民户 外活动的条件,又使城市更加美丽 是补充结果。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 定语 过去分词;既…又… 并列谓语 '政府出资购置的''铺设的'两个定语用过去分词降级:fitness equipment funded by the government and fitness trails it has paved(或合并为 government-funded fitness equipment and paved trails)。句末 既明显改善了市民户外活动的条件,又使城市更加美丽 是'随处可见'带来的 双重效果,用 which 引导的非限定定语从句 + 并列谓语收尾:which not only … but also …,避免另 起流水句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 '随处可见'是现状 现在时 can be seen / are commonly seen;'改善了'带完成义可用现在完成时 have improved,与基调不冲突。 语态 '随处可见''出资购置的''铺设的'都隐含被动(被看见/被购置/被铺设),英文用被动 can be seen / funded by / paved,符合英文被动多于汉语的习惯。 单复数 fitness equipment 是不可数名词,作主语时谓语单复数取决于并列:equipment and trails 两者并 列 谓语用复数 are / can be seen;trails 用复数。 关联词 '既…又…'用 not only … but also …;若 not only 提到句首需部分倒装,放从句中部则不倒装,本句用 which not only improves … but also makes … 不倒装更稳。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Today, government-funded fitness equipment and newly paved fitness trails can be seen everywhere in many cities, which has not only markedly improved the conditions for residents' outdoor activities but also made cities more beautiful. 英语六级 2023年6月·第2套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
